questions.question: Which characteristic of the CPU determines how many instructions it can process per second?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Clock Speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Clock speed** is the rate at which a CPU executes instructions, measured in **Hertz (Hz)**, typically in **gigahertz (GHz)** for modern processors.
 
• It determines how many **cycles per second** the CPU can perform, directly impacting the number of instructions it can process per second.
 
• Higher clock speeds generally lead to **faster processing** and improved performance in computational tasks.
 
• Clock speed is a critical factor in determining the overall **performance** of a CPU, especially for tasks requiring high computational power.
 
• Modern CPUs also utilize techniques like **turbo boost** to temporarily increase clock speed for demanding applications.
 
• However, clock speed alone doesn’t determine performance; it must be combined with other factors like **core count** and **architecture efficiency**.
 
• A CPU with a higher clock speed but fewer cores may perform better for single-threaded tasks, while multi-core CPUs are better for multi-threaded applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Power Consumption**__

 __
 
• **Power consumption** refers to the amount of electrical energy the CPU uses during its operation.
 
• It has an impact on **heat generation** and the need for cooling solutions but does not directly determine the number of instructions a CPU can process per second.
 
• Efficient CPUs balance power consumption and performance for tasks like mobile devices and laptops.
 
 
 
• **Cache Size**__
 __
 
• **Cache size** refers to the amount of high-speed memory available on the CPU for storing frequently used data.
 
• A larger cache can improve **performance** by reducing the need to access slower main memory, but it doesn’t directly define how many instructions can be processed per second.
 
• It plays a crucial role in reducing **latency** and improving data retrieval speeds.
 
 
 
• **Number of Registers**__
 
 
• The **number of registers** refers to the small amount of memory within the CPU used to store data temporarily during execution.
 
• While registers are essential for efficient data processing, their count doesn’t directly determine the CPU's ability to process instructions per second.
 
• Registers are vital for tasks like **arithmetic operations** and **instruction decoding**.

questions.question: If you want your audience to NOT see your notes in the MS PowerPoint 365 slides, which view should you use during slide show?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Presenter View** is a feature in **MS PowerPoint 365** that allows the presenter to see notes and other tools on their screen while the audience only sees the slide presentation.
 
• In **Presenter View**, the presenter has access to **tools** such as a timer, navigation controls, and the ability to view their speaker notes privately.
 
• This mode is particularly useful for maintaining a **professional presentation flow** while keeping key notes and details for the presenter out of the audience's view.
 
• **Presenter View** typically requires a dual-monitor setup, where one monitor displays the presentation for the audience, and the other monitor shows the **notes and controls for the presenter.**
 
• It enhances the **engagement** and **confidence** of the presenter by providing a clear view of their notes and upcoming slides.
 
• To enable **Presenter View**, go to the **Slide Show** tab, and then check the box labeled "**Use Presenter View**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Outline View**__

 __
 
• The **Outline View** in PowerPoint shows the **text content of slides** in an outline format.
 
• It is commonly used for editing and organizing content but is not suitable for hiding notes during a presentation.
 
 
 
• **Slide Show View**__
 __
 
• The **Slide Show View** is used to display slides to the audience in full-screen mode.
 
• While this view does not show notes to the audience, it also does not allow the presenter to view their notes privately, unlike **Presenter View**.
 
 
 
• **Reading View**__
 
 
• The **Reading View** displays the presentation in a **windowed format** and is useful for reviewing the presentation on a single screen.
 
• It does not provide tools for presenting with notes hidden from the audience.

questions.question: Which of the following brings winter rainfall to northern plains of India?

__
 
• **Western disturbances** are extratropical storms originating in the **Mediterranean region**.
 
• They travel eastward and bring **winter rainfall** to the **northern plains of India**, particularly in **Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• These disturbances are caused due to the westerly winds in the upper atmosphere, which carry moisture from the **Mediterranean Sea**, the **Atlantic Ocean**, and sometimes even from the **Caspian Sea**.
 
• The rainfall brought by these disturbances is crucial for the **rabi crops**, especially **wheat**, in northern India.
 
• They usually occur during the **winter months**, from December to February, though they can sometimes extend into early March.
 
• The interaction of Western disturbances with the Himalayas often leads to snowfall in the **higher altitudes** and rainfall in the plains.
 
• This phenomenon plays a significant role in maintaining the **climate balance** in the region by lowering temperatures and providing moisture.
 
• Western disturbances are also responsible for causing **cold waves** in northern India during winters.

 __
 
• **Norwesters**, also called **Kalbaisakhi** in India, are thunderstorms that occur during the **pre-monsoon season**, mainly in **eastern India**, such as West Bengal, Assam, and Odisha.
 
• These storms are characterized by strong winds, heavy rainfall, and sometimes hailstorms, but they are not responsible for winter rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Bay of Bengal cyclones**__

• These cyclones are responsible for heavy rainfall in the eastern coastal states of India but do not impact the winter rainfall in northern plains.
 
 
 
• **Easterlies**__
 
 
• **Easterlies** are trade winds that blow from the east to the west in the **tropical regions**.
 
• They are associated with the monsoon season in India and do not contribute to winter rainfall in the northern plains.

questions.question: According to Article 246 of the Indian Constitution, parliament has exclusive powers to make laws on subjects mentioned in which of the following lists?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Union List**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 246** of the Indian Constitution specifies the legislative powers of the Union and State governments.
 
• The **Union List** includes subjects on which only the **Parliament** has the exclusive power to legislate.
 
• Examples of subjects in the **Union List** include **defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, railways, banking, and communication.**
 
• This exclusive power ensures a unified approach to critical subjects that impact the entire country.
 
• The **Union List** presently consists of **97 subjects** (as per the original Constitution, though amendments may have altered the number).
 
• It is crucial for maintaining the **sovereignty and integrity** of India by centralizing decision-making on essential matters.
 
• The subjects in the Union List are designed to address areas of national importance and ensure uniformity in governance across states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **State List**__

 __
 
• The **State List** includes subjects on which **State Legislatures** have exclusive power to legislate.
 
• Examples include **police, public health, agriculture, and local governments.**
 
• This list allows states to govern matters that are primarily regional in nature.
 
 
 
• **Local List**__
 __
 
• The term **Local List** is not officially recognized within the Indian Constitution.
 
• Local governance is primarily addressed through the **Panchayati Raj system** under the **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments.**
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List**__
 
 
• The **Concurrent List** includes subjects on which both the **Parliament and State Legislatures** can legislate.
 
• Examples include **education, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy, and adoption.**
 
• In case of a conflict, the law made by the **Parliament** prevails over the State law.

questions.question: Which gas is a major product of industrial production for use in aerosol propellants and air conditioning systems?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Freon-12**__.

__
 
• **Freon-12** is a type of chlorofluorocarbon (**CFC**) commonly used as an aerosol propellant and refrigerant.
 
• It is scientifically known as **Dichlorodifluoromethane**, with the chemical formula **CCl₂F₂**.
 
• Freon-12 was extensively used in **industrial production** for applications such as **air conditioning systems**, refrigeration, and aerosol sprays.
 
• Its widespread use was due to its **non-flammable** and **stable chemical properties**, making it safe for various applications.
 
• However, the use of Freon-12 and other CFCs has been significantly reduced because they contribute to the **depletion of the ozone layer**.
 
• The **Montreal Protocol**, an international treaty signed in **1987**, aims to phase out substances like Freon-12 that harm the ozone layer.
 
• Freon-12's alternatives, such as **hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)**, are now being used in many industries to minimize environmental damage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Oxygen**__

 __
 
• **Oxygen** is a vital gas for the **sustenance of life** on Earth.
 
• It constitutes about **21%** of Earth's atmosphere.
 
• Industrial applications of oxygen include **steel manufacturing, welding, and medical uses** like oxygen therapy.
 
• It is not primarily used in aerosol propellants or air conditioning systems.
 
 
 
• **Methane**__
 __
 
• **Methane** is a **natural gas** primarily used as a fuel for heating and electricity generation.
 
• It is also a significant greenhouse gas contributing to **global warming**.
 
• Methane is not suitable for use as an aerosol propellant or refrigerant.
 
 
 
• **Carbon monoxide**__
 
 
• **Carbon monoxide** is a toxic gas produced by **incomplete combustion** of carbon-based fuels.
 
• It is used in **industrial processes** like the production of chemicals and metal extraction.
 
• Due to its toxicity, it is not used in applications like aerosol propellants or air conditioning systems.

• When a string is plucked, the **up-and-down motion** of the string creates a wave pattern where the crests and troughs are visible.
 
• The wave travels along the length of the string, but the **displacement** of the string particles is at right angles to this direction.
 
• This type of wave is characterized by **wavelength, frequency, amplitude,** and speed.
 
• Examples of transverse waves include **light waves, water waves**, and waves on a string.
 
• Such waves do not require a medium for propagation (if electromagnetic), but on a string, they propagate through the medium of the string material.

• **Electromagnetic wave**__

questions.question: Which of the following is an incorrect statement about Cache Memory?

options.text: Cache memory is faster than main memory.
Cache memory stores frequently accessed data for quick retrieval.
Cache memory is a form of secondary storage.
Cache memory is located close to or inside the CPU.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Cache memory is a form of secondary storage.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cache memory** is a type of **volatile memory** that provides high-speed data access to the processor.
 
• It is designed to store **frequently accessed data** or instructions so that the processor can retrieve them quickly without accessing slower main memory (RAM).
 
• Cache memory is located **closer to or inside the CPU**, reducing the time taken to fetch data.
 
• Cache memory is significantly **faster than main memory (RAM)**, but it is smaller in size and more expensive.
 
• It is not a form of **secondary storage**. Secondary storage refers to devices like **hard drives, SSDs, and external storage**, which are used for permanent data storage and are slower than both cache and main memory.
 
• The primary goal of cache memory is to **enhance the speed and efficiency** of the CPU by minimizing data access delays.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cache memory is faster than main memory.**__

 __
 
• **Cache memory** operates at a much higher speed compared to **RAM**, allowing the CPU to process instructions faster.
 
• It uses technologies like **SRAM (Static RAM)**, which is faster than DRAM (used in main memory).
 
 
 
• **Cache memory stores frequently accessed data for quick retrieval.**__
 __
 
• **Cache memory** identifies and temporarily stores **data or instructions** that are frequently used by the CPU.
 
• This minimizes the need to access slower main memory repeatedly, enhancing overall system performance.
 
 
 
• **Cache memory is located close to or inside the CPU.**__
 
 
• Cache memory is either **embedded inside the CPU** (e.g., L1 and L2 cache) or placed **very close to the CPU** (e.g., L3 cache).
 
• This proximity reduces latency, allowing the processor to access data faster.
